setup_summary.text: PANW is scheduled to report fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter ended Oct 31, 2026) on 2026-11-12, time unknown. Consensus is EPS $0.99 and revenue $3.37B.

Q4 FY26 was a beat and a re-acceleration. Revenue was $3.41B (+34%), and non-GAAP EPS of $1.02 exceeded the top of the guided range by $0.04. NGS ARR reached $9.1B (+63%) with nearly $1B of net new ARR in the quarter. RPO was $21.2B (+34%).

FY26 GAAP profitability was weak even as revenue grew. Revenue was $11.48B (+24.5%), but operating income fell 44% to $695M (6.1% margin). Net income was $307M and diluted EPS $0.40 versus $1.60. Derived Q4 GAAP operating income was $172M (5.0% margin) and net loss was $282M.

The GAAP drag comes from acquisition accounting and non-cash items. FY26 intangible amortization was $640M, with $1.08B scheduled for FY27. Share-based compensation was $1.815B. A $620M fair-value loss on the CyberArk 2030 convertible notes was partly offset by a $58M Capped Call gain. Gross margin fell to 70.4% from 73.4%.

Reported growth is flattered by M&A. The 10-K pro forma revenue is $12.31B for FY26 versus $10.49B for FY25, about +17%, versus +24.5% reported. Q1 FY27 laps a year-ago quarter of $2.47B that had no CyberArk or Chronosphere, so the guided +33-34% is largely inorganic.

Q1 guidance is revenue $3.30-3.31B, non-GAAP EPS $0.96-0.98, NGS ARR $9.54-9.56B and RPO $20.8-20.9B. Finnhub consensus (revenue $3.37B, EPS $0.99) sits above the top of the revenue and EPS guidance ranges. Zacks consensus ($3.31B, $0.97) is in line with guidance.

The stock has run hard but has recently pulled back. Seeking Alpha says it is up 90% in 2026 at about 84x earnings. Market cap was about $319B on Oct 28. Tradingkey reports declines of 5.26% on Oct 29 and 4.12% on Oct 30. Fortinet fell sharply after its Q3 print on a beat, though the cause of PANW's drop is not sourced.
The average closing move over the last 8 reports is about ±5.1%. No options-implied move is available.

metrics_to_model.metric: NGS ARR and net new NGS ARR

last_reported.text: NGS ARR was $9.1B at Q4 (+63%), with nearly $1B of net new in the quarter. That included a nine-figure benefit from a large LLM customer migrating to Chronosphere.

view.text: Guidance of $9.54-9.56B implies about $0.44-0.46B of net new ARR, less than half of Q4. Management says Q1 will be larger than normal because of the migration tail, with 60-61% of FY27 net new ARR in 2H. A result at or above $9.56B with no migration step-down would be constructive. Chronosphere ARR and any disclosure of the migration's contribution are the swing items.

Q1 RPO guidance of $20.8-20.9B is below the $21.2B year-end level, implying a sequential decline. Watch for a beat versus guidance and whether bookings growth, which management says accelerated for a second quarter, holds up on a pro forma basis. Contract duration is described as steady.

last_reported.text: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 74.8% (down 100bp y/y). FY26 was 75.8% (down 60bp). GAAP FY26 gross margin was 70.4%.

view.text: Management expects cloud hosting costs to grow faster than revenue in FY27 and memory/storage costs to persist in hardware (about 10% of revenue). The 10-K cites the Q4 supply chain disruption and memory shortage. Expect further y/y compression, with the debate over whether operating leverage offsets it.

metrics_to_model.metric: Non-GAAP operating margin and adjusted FCF margin

last_reported.text: Q4 non-GAAP operating margin was 29.6% and FY26 was 29.2%. FY26 adjusted FCF was $4.41B (38.4% margin). The 10-K shows FCF of $4.11B on a GAAP-reconciled basis.

view.text: FY27 guidance is 29.5% operating margin and 38% adjusted FCF margin. Management says CyberArk synergies are 3-6 months ahead of plan. The 29.5% guide is only about 30bp above FY26 despite full-year consolidation of lower-margin acquired businesses. Q1 non-GAAP operating margin versus 29.5% is the check.

metrics_to_model.metric: Revenue by platform (Network & AI Security, Cortex, Idira)

last_reported.text: FY26 revenue: Network & AI Security $8.35B (+17%), including about $85M from NGTS. Cortex $1.92B (+25%). Idira pro forma $1.26B (+21%).

view.text: FY27 modeling points are Network & AI Security low double-digit growth, Cortex about +30%, and Idira about $1.5B (high teens to 20% pro forma growth). This is the first quarter with platform disclosure, so expect scrutiny of any shortfall versus these trajectories. Network & AI Security at low double digits is slower than the 17% FY26 growth, which includes NGTS.

metrics_to_model.metric: GAAP diluted EPS and below-the-line items

last_reported.text: Q4 net loss was derived at $282M (-8.3% margin). FY26 diluted EPS was $0.40, hit by a $620M fair-value loss on the 2030 Notes and a 42.7% effective tax rate.

view.text: GAAP EPS will be driven by fair-value marks on the $1.1B 2030 Notes (fair value $1.8B at year-end) and Capped Calls, which move with the stock price. Year-end RSU intrinsic value implies about $329/share at 7/31 (5,594/17, rounded inputs), versus $380.55 on Oct 23. That suggests another fair-value loss is plausible, though the Oct 31 price is unknown.

last_reported.text: Q4 had about 22 net new platformizations, with NRR above 120% in the platformized cohort. Prisma AIRS ARR exceeded $100M. XSIAM ARR exceeded $700M (+70%). Observability ARR exceeded $500M.

view.text: The long-term targets are over 4,000 platformizations and $20B NGS ARR by FY30. Sustaining 20+ net new platformizations per quarter and continued XSIAM/AIRS growth supports the guide. These KPIs are management-defined and not audited.

since_filing.text: There is no company disclosure after the 10-K in the sources. The earnings call transcript is dated 2026-09-01, before the 10-K filing on 2026-09-10, so all guidance is as of Sept 1. The 10-K confirms the Embrace (Aug 27) and Console (Sept 1) acquisitions closed, consistent with the call.

Stock moves: PANW rose 7.22% to $380.55 on Oct 23 after three straight gains. Tradingkey then reports declines of 5.26% on Oct 29 and 4.12% on Oct 30. Fortinet plunged after its Q3 results despite beating (EPS $0.91 vs $0.85, revenue +20% to $2.08B). The peer sell-off may have weighed on PANW, but no source links the two.
Sentiment is mixed. Seeking Alpha (Oct 22) argues that 34% growth is really about 15% organic at 84x earnings. This is consistent with the 10-K pro forma growth of about 17%.

Consensus sources differ. Zacks (Oct 27) expects EPS $0.97 and revenue $3.31B (+33.6%), in line with guidance. Finnhub shows $0.99 and $3.37B, above the guidance ranges. The next report's bar depends on which is closer to the buy side.

Basis reconciliation between the call and the 10-K. The call's gross margin (75.8% FY, 74.8% Q4), operating margin (29.2%) and adjusted FCF ($4.41B) are non-GAAP. The 10-K shows GAAP gross margin of 70.4%, operating margin of 6.1% and FCF of $4.11B. These are different bases, not contradictions. The 10-K is the more reliable tier for GAAP figures.

key_debates.question: Is the growth durable and organic, or acquisition-driven?

bull.text: Bookings growth accelerated for a second quarter on a pro forma basis. NGS ARR is up 63%. Platformized cohort NRR is above 120%. Idira and Chronosphere are exceeding expectations, and SASE bookings grew 40% with about $450M of competitive displacements.

bear.text: Pro forma FY26 revenue growth is about 17%, and FY27 guided growth of 23-24% is boosted by acquisition annualization. Network & AI Security is guided to low double-digit growth, and Q1 growth of 33-34% mostly reflects M&A.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Pro forma or organic growth disclosure, Q1 NGS ARR net new versus the roughly $0.45B implied, and Network & AI Security growth versus the 'low double digit' guide.

key_debates.question: Can margins hold at 29.5% non-GAAP with gross margin under pressure?

bull.text: Synergies are 3-6 months ahead of plan. Q4 non-GAAP operating margin was 29.6%, up 40bp y/y for the year. Management says operating leverage will more than offset higher COGS.

bear.text: GAAP gross margin fell about 300bp to 70.4% and GAAP operating margin was 6.1%. Cloud hosting is growing faster than revenue, memory costs are rising, cloud purchase commitments total $7.7B, and SBC of $1.8B is excluded from the non-GAAP margin.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q1 non-GAAP gross margin and operating margin versus the 29.5% FY guide, and any change in FY27 margin guidance.

key_debates.question: Is the stock's expectation bar too high after the run-up?

bull.text: Management says it sets guidance to exceed consensus. Q4 beat on every metric, with revenue $60M and EPS $0.04 above consensus.

bear.text: Finnhub consensus revenue of $3.37B and EPS of $0.99 sit above the top of guidance ($3.31B, $0.98). The stock is reportedly up about 90% in 2026 at about 84x earnings, and fell about 9% over Oct 29-30. The average post-earnings move is ±5.1%.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The print versus the $3.37B and $0.99 consensus (not just guidance), and whether FY27 guidance is raised by more than the Q1 beat.

key_debates.question: How durable is the Chronosphere and consumption-based ARR?

bull.text: Observability ARR more than doubled to over $500M since close, and management says it is competitive on price, 30-40% cheaper than incumbents. XSIAM and observability together exceed $1B ARR.

bear.text: Q4 net new ARR included a nine-figure benefit from one large LLM customer migration, which tapers in Q1. The 10-K warns of customer optimization behavior in consumption-based and AI-native cohorts.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q1 net new NGS ARR versus about $0.45B implied, Chronosphere ARR trend, and any commentary on large-customer concentration or usage optimization.

claim.text: Expectation risk. Finnhub consensus revenue ($3.37B) and EPS ($0.99) exceed the top of guidance, and the stock is reportedly up about 90% YTD at about 84x earnings. A beat versus guidance may not be enough.

Customer optimization and concentration in consumption-based offerings. The 10-K flags AI-native and large-enterprise cohorts for usage reductions, and Q4 ARR included a nine-figure single-LLM-customer migration that tapers in Q1.
Gross margin pressure from cloud hosting growth, memory and component shortages, tariffs, and amortization. Cloud purchase commitments total $7.7B.
The product vulnerability disclosed in May 2026 (a PAN-OS authentication bypass), plus the general risk of security incidents, defects and false positives, could harm reputation and renewals.

Integration and M&A risk. The company closed CyberArk ($21.1B), Chronosphere ($3.0B), Koi, Portkey, Embrace and Console in about eight months. It carries $22.0B of goodwill and $7.0B of intangibles with no impairment to date. The 10-K's audit matter flags the $3.5B platform renewals valuation as a judgment area.

Convertible notes. $1.1B of 2030 Notes could become convertible and settle in cash if the $280.75 stock price condition is met. The condition was not met for the June 2026 quarter. Fair-value moves create GAAP volatility (a $620M loss in FY26) and the notes affect the tax rate.

Competition and AI disruption. Hyperscalers and frontier AI labs may offer native security and observability, and market perception of AI commoditizing cybersecurity could weigh on the stock regardless of fundamentals. Vendor consolidation may also favor broader platforms.

Distribution concentration. Two distributors represented 30% of FY26 revenue and one represented 19% of gross accounts receivable. Customer financing receivables total about $1.5B, and Israel operations expanded with CyberArk.

questions_for_management.question: What was Q1 net new NGS ARR excluding the LLM-customer Chronosphere migration, and how concentrated is Chronosphere ARR in AI-native customers?

why.text: Q4's nearly $1B of net new ARR included a nine-figure single-customer benefit, and Q1 guidance implies only about $0.45B. The 10-K flags optimization risk.

questions_for_management.question: What are pro forma or organic growth rates for revenue, bookings and RPO, and how much of the FY27 guidance depends on acquisition annualization?

why.text: Reported growth of 33-34% is flattered by acquisitions, while pro forma FY26 growth is about 17%. Investors are debating the quality of the growth rate.

questions_for_management.question: How should we model gross margin through FY27 given hosting costs rising faster than revenue and memory/storage costs? How much do selective hardware price increases offset?

why.text: Non-GAAP gross margin was down 100bp in Q4. The 10-K describes memory shortages, and management says hosting cost growth will outpace revenue.

questions_for_management.question: Did the 2030 Notes' sale price condition get met in the September quarter, and what is the plan and cash impact if holders convert? Does the balance-sheet classification change?

why.text: If the $280.75 condition was met, the notes could become convertible in the Dec quarter with $1.1B principal settled in cash, and the stock traded well above that level. GAAP EPS is highly sensitive to the fair-value marks.

questions_for_management.question: What explains the gap between the 818M shares outstanding and the 844-847M FY27 diluted guide? What are your buyback plans, given $1.0B of authorization expiring Dec 31, 2026 and no Q4 repurchases?

why.text: Dilution and buyback intent affect EPS comparisons. The Q1 share count in the transcript is garbled.

questions_for_management.question: What is the effect of the May PAN-OS vulnerability on renewals, product trust or remediation cost? Does the increased shift to annual billing (about 30% of bookings) affect cash flow or RPO duration?

why.text: The 10-K calls out the May 2026 authentication bypass. Billing mix shifts affect FCF and RPO comparisons, and the FCF margin is guided to 38% (40% by FY28).

questions_for_management.question: Are Idira cross-sell and Modern PAM upgrades tracking to the roughly $1.5B revenue and high-teens to 20% pro forma growth guide, and how do hyperscaler and frontier AI competition in identity and observability affect pricing?

why.text: Idira is the largest acquisition, and the 10-K raises incremental competition and the lack of a standard identity security market definition.

The reason for the Oct 29-30 share declines is not sourced. The link to Fortinet's results is an inference.
Prior-year risk factors were not provided, so the is_new flags on key risks are a judgment based on whether the risk references FY26 events.
The XBRL fact sheet reports no long-term debt tag (F.14), though the balance sheet shows $1,774M of long-term convertible senior notes at fair value.
Fiscal Q2 FY27 will still include a partial inorganic benefit from CyberArk (closed Feb 2026) and Chronosphere (closed Jan 2026). A true organic growth rate is not disclosed in the sources.
